title: Coverage of essential health services
national_indicator_description: This indicator is an index combining 14 tracer indicators in four general categories: (1) Reproductive, maternal, newborn and child health; (2) Infectious diseases; (3) Noncommunicable diseases; and (4) Service capacity and access.
computation_definitions: Coverage of essential health services is defined as the average coverage of essential services based on tracer interventions that include reproductive, maternal, newborn and child health, infectious diseases, non-communicable diseases and service capacity and access, among the general and the most disadvantaged population.
computation_calculations: This indicator is an index computed as the weighted geometric means of 14 tracer indicators. Please see the Global Metadata tab for a link to more information on the tracer indicators and methodology used.
other_info: This indicator uses data from a number of different sources. The principal sources are listed under the Sources tab on this page, however, sources for some tracer indicators are missing or incomplete. Some additional information on sources is available for tracer indicators which also correspond to another SDG indicator; please see the pages for indicators [3.7.1](https://sustainabledevelopment-rwanda.github.io/3-7-1/), [3.a.1](https://sustainabledevelopment-rwanda.github.io/3-a-1/), [3.c.1](https://sustainabledevelopment-rwanda.github.io/3-c-1/), and [3.d.1](https://sustainabledevelopment-rwanda.github.io/3-d-1/) for more information on sources used for the corresponding tracer indicators.
comments_limitations: The 14 tracer indicators used to calculate this indicator include different sources with different methodologies, including different survey populations, resulting in some level of imprecision.
target_name: Achieve universal health coverage, including financial risk protection, access to quality essential health-care services and access to safe, effective, quality and affordable essential medicines and vaccines for all
indicator_definition: Coverage of essential health services (defined as the average coverage of essential services based on tracer interventions that include reproductive, maternal, newborn and child health, infectious diseases, non-communicable diseases and service capacity and access, among the general and the most disadvantaged population).
goal_meta_link_text: United Nations Sustainable Development Goals Metadata (pdf 865kB)
source_organisation_1: National Institute of Statistics of Rwanda (NISR)
source_other_info_1: This source contains data for the following tracer indicators: Percentage of women of reproductive age (15−49 years) who have their need for family planning satisfied with modern methods; Percentage of women aged 15-49 years with a live birth in a given time period who received antenatal care four or more times; Percentage of infants receiving three doses of diphtheria-tetanus-pertussis containing vaccine; Percentage of children younger than 5 years with symptoms of acute respiratory infection (cough and fast or difficult breathing due to a problem in the chest and not due to a blocked nose only) in the 2 weeks preceding the survey for whom advice or treatment was sought from a health facility or provider; Percentage of incident TB cases that are detected and treated; Percentage of population in malaria-endemic areas who slept under an insecticide-treated net the previous night; Percentage of population using at least basic sanitation services; and Age-standardized prevalence of adults >=15 years currently using any tobacco product (smoked and/or smokeless tobacco) on a daily or non-daily basis. The [Statistical Yearbook](https://statistics.gov.rw/statistical-publications/statistical-yearbook), also prepared by the National Institute of Statistics of Rwanda (NISR), further contains data for the tracer indicator Health workers per capita. Furthermore, the [Population and Housing Census](https://statistics.gov.rw/data-sources/censuses/Population-and-Housing-Census) contains population data used for the denominator of several indicators.
source_other_info_2: This source contains data for the following tracer indicators: Percentage of population in malaria-endemic areas who slept under an insecticide-treated net the previous night ([Malaria and Neglected Tropical Diseases Annual Report](https://rbc.gov.rw/fileadmin/user_upload/report_2026/MOPDD_Annual_Report_FY2024-2025%20Final.pdf)); Coverage of treatment (taking medicine) for hypertension among adults aged 30-79 years with hypertension ([Public Health Bulletin](https://rbc.gov.rw/publichealthbulletin/img/rphb_issues/RPHB%206%20(3)%20REPORTS%20ISSUE%20updated.pdf)); and Coverage of treatment (taking medication) for diabetes among adults aged 30 years and over with diabetes ([STEPS Booklet](https://www.rbc.gov.rw/fileadmin/user_upload/report23/STEPS%20Booklet.pdf)).
source_other_info_3: This source contains data for the tracer indicator Health workers (medical doctors, nursing and midwifery personnel) per capita. Most of the data are sourced from the [Annual Health Statistical Booklet](https://www.moh.gov.rw/fileadmin/user_upload/Moh/Publications/Reports/new_annual_Report/Annual_Statistical_Booklet_Fiscal_Year_2023-2024_Final_10102025.pdf), although some data are also sourced from the [Backward-Looking Joint Health Sector Review Meeting Report](https://moh.prod.risa.rw/fileadmin/user_upload/Moh/Publications/Reports/2022_23_BLJSR_24112023_Final_ABM_and_PS_Signed.pdf). Further data for this indicator is available from the [Statistical Yearbook](https://statistics.gov.rw/statistical-publications/statistical-yearbook) prepared by the National Institute of Statistics of Rwanda (NISR), particularly for the years 2012-2015.
source_url_text_4: Electronic IHR States Parties Self-Assessment Annual Reporting Tool
source_other_info_4: This source contains data for the International Health Regulations (IHR) core capacity index, which is the average percentage of attributes of 15 core capacities that have been attained. The [WHO Data Portal](https://data.who.int/countries/646) further contains additional or alternative estimates relevant to several tracer indicators.
source_other_info_5: This source contains data for the tracer indicator Hospital beds density. Other pages on the World Bank data portal also provide additional or alternative estimates relevant to several tracer indicators.
